walkthroughs.body_html:
The Petrarchan sonnet rhymes ABBAABBA in the octave then CDECDE or CDCDCD in the sestet, with the volta at line 9.

Shakespearean sonnets rhyme ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often deploying the closing couplet as a witty summative turn.
In 1819 Keats produced odes on Indolence, Psyche, a Nightingale, a Grecian Urn, Melancholy and Autumn — sustained address combining sensuous imagery with philosophical meditation.
The traditional elegiac arc moves from grief through philosophical confrontation toward consolation. Tennyson's In Memoriam (1850) marshals 133 sections of grief for Hallam.
